The part of a tree that grows underground is the roots.

Based on the contextual clues provided in the text, the time period is the 19th century, specifically the Victorian era (roughly 1837–1901). The presence of horse-drawn carriages and gas lighting indicates a pre-electric, pre-automotive urban environment. The architectural styles of Georgian and Victorian further narrow the timeframe to the 18th and 19th centuries. Most definitively, the mention of Charles Dickens as a contemporary figure whose works are "the talk of the town" places the setting firmly in the mid-to-late 19th century, as Dickens was most prominent during the Victorian era.
